convoLines.text: "Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
"Here's what I think — I regret the ordinary days I rushed through. All those Columbus, Ohio mornings I spent annoyed at small things. I'd pay anything for one annoyed morning now."
"Still on your regrets."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Chorus Line? I'm pushing 'The Ugly Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
You show them Goldenrod — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"Good. I mean it — watch yourself out there."
"I keep thinking about that Loud-Eyes. It knows this ground now. Keep your eyes up past the treeline."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"The whole fire was arguing about Chorus Line last night — what to even CALL it. 'Don't-Look' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said there was something you needed to say, to someone, and now you can't. Found another way to say it yet?"
There's an ease between you now — the kind that takes weeks to build.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff. I mean it."
They take it in and give nothing back. Not yet.
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Right — go on, I'm listening."
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Since Caroline died... I keep expecting to see Caroline at the fire. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Brunhilde grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Oliver is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I sit apart to eat for Caroline, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Sure. I'll be around."

"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'Okay. We'll pick this up later.'"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
"Here. I made an extra." Brunhilde presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"I save the best bite for last. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
They hear you out, but something in them stays guarded.

Oliver nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)

"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."

"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."

Their whole posture softens around you.

Row on row of them, humming like a held note -- and I wake up reaching for something that isn't there."

"Thao was my person at this fire. I keep turning to the wrong empty spot."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."

"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."

"Rest and clean water aren't cutting it. If this turns, I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. I need someone who knows what they're doing."

"Still on that sickness help."

Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."

"Hot showers. Not the big things — the small, stupid, perfect things. Cape Town, South Africa in the morning, coffee going, nobody trying to kill me. I miss being bored. No time to waste."

"Still on what you miss most. But what do I know."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"I wasn't an EMT. I was a taxi driver. I was ashamed of the truth. Out here nobody asks, so I stopped telling."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Thabo rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
Thabo looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
Mia nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)

"I don't do parties. ...It's not you. It's the party."

"Since Oliver died... I keep expecting to see Oliver at the fire. Stupid."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."

"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"See you around."

lines: d31: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Caroline Mejia is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d31: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d31: 🕯️ Caroline Mejia is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d31: What Caroline kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d31: "Caroline's gone." Oliver looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Caroline." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d31: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Thao blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d31: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d31: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d31: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d31: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Caroline Mejia, 31 days. The mantle passes to Thao Prince.
d31: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Thao Prince, 27 — a Vintner. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper.
d31: The village's quarrel was with Caroline — and Caroline is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d31: At the grave, Oliver, Brunhilde, Estela and 3 more speak for Thao — "Caroline trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d31: The fire knew Thao before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
d67: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Thao Prince is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d67: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
